channel.title: Nerazzurri Daily
channel.description: Inter Milan in English, every morning, in 90 seconds — what the club has confirmed, kept apart from what the papers are only reporting.

item.title: Italy lose 0–2 to Belgium with two Inter men starting
item.description: Lega Serie A has confirmed Inter's dates and kickoff times through matchday 19, and the Coppa Italia last 16 against Genoa is on the calendar too.

item.title: Inter's board signs off a €22.7 million profit
item.description: Nicolò Barella and Francesco Pio Esposito are in Italy's squad for tonight's Nations League opener in Rome, where a minute's silence will remember Sandro Mazzola.

item.title: Thirteen Inter players are away with their countries
item.description: Inter Women open their Serie A season on Sunday at the Arena Civica in Milan, and admission is free.

item.title: Inter Women win their Champions League debut, 1–0
item.description: Haley Bugeja scored in the fifth minute at the Stadio Brianteo in Monza, and Inter came out of the opening round third in the league phase.

item.title: Milan says goodbye to Mazzola, and Inter Women debut today
item.description: Inter Women play their first Champions League match today against BK Häcken of Sweden, and Federico Dimarco has left Italy's camp with a knee problem.

item.title: Inter Women's Champions League debut is Tuesday
item.description: Inter U23 beat Foggia 3–2 for a second straight win, and thirteen first-team players have left for national duty during the three-week break.

item.title: Lautaro scores twice as Inter draw 2–2 at the Olimpico
item.description: Manu Koné put Roma two goals up inside 37 minutes; Inter and Roma go into a three-week international break level at the top of Serie A with 13 points each.

item.title: Sandro Mazzola dies, aged 83
item.description: Sandro Mazzola has died, aged 83. Inter play Roma at the Olimpico with both clubs level on 12 points, and the club names John Stones's injury.

item.title: Stones' left hamstring, and a silent Chivu
item.description: The club names John Stones's injury as a left hamstring strain, Davide Massa referees at the Olimpico, and the women's season gets its dates.

item.title: Stones scanned this morning
item.description: John Stones goes for scans this morning, a day later than the papers first had it. Inter Women open their Champions League at Monza on Tuesday, and Davide Massa takes Roma–Inter on Saturday.

item.title: Çalhanoğlu's adductor, and a scan for Stones
item.description: Inter confirm an adductor strain for Hakan Çalhanoğlu, Sky Sport Italia aims him at the Parma match, Gazzetta expects John Stones back after the international break, and Genoa are Inter's Coppa Italia opponents.

item.title: Inter 5–3 Udinese, from two down
item.description: Inter came from two goals down to beat Udinese 5–3 at San Siro. Chivu took the blame and defended his goalkeeper; Sky has Stones and Çalhanoğlu in doubt for Roma.

item.title: Stones in, Dimarco benched
item.description: Chivu confirms Dimarco is available and Spence is not, Sky's projected lineup gives John Stones his first Inter start, and the new third kit plays tonight against Udinese.

item.title: Dimarco available
item.description: Sky has Federico Dimarco back in full group training and available for Udinese on Monday; Chivu speaks at 8:00 AM ET; Inter Women open in Europe on September 22.

item.title: Dimarco talks open
item.description: Saturday, September 12, 2026: Gazzetta dello Sport reports Inter have opened talks on a contract to 2030 for Federico Dimarco, Chivu's press conference is set for Sunday, and John Stones is in line to start against Udinese.

item.title: Stones in, Dimarco close
item.description: Friday, September 11, 2026: Gazzetta reports John Stones starting at center back against Udinese with Akanji at right back, Sky has Dimarco close to full training, and Inter Women extend Polli and Robustellini to 2029.
